title: Back up your data
body: I had been using Way of Life daily for over four years to track all of my habits, including medications. I loved using the app and it worked great, until one day I downloaded an update and all of my data disappeared. I incorrectly believed that the data was linked to my account, when it actually is not linked to anything at all and needed to be manually backed up in order to be saved. I was super disappointed by this, as I lost many streaks of over 1000 days, as well as important medical information, because this information was not shared anywhere. I think it is a great app to use for habits if you’re willing to manually backed-up your data on a regular basis, but I will be switching to an app that actually stores the data in your account so you do not have to take this extra step.

title: LOCKED OUT OF APP
body:
I am locked out of my app 😡 and have zero way to get back in.

I saw there was a password protection feature so I wanted to try it.

It was asking me to put a pin password in on a numeric keypad. At first I put in a pin and I did put it in a second time to confirm it because I saw there was a faceID button and I preferred that over a pin. 

The app LET ME register FaceID WITHOUT registering a pin password, and under the password section I saw FaceID listed there with a toggle button to turn it on and off. 

Then I decided I didn’t like it and wanted to turn FACEID off so turned off the toggle button off for FaceID. I ASSUMED that this meant the password was off since I was allowed to register FACEID WITHOUT registering a pin.

Now every time I open the app all I see is a keypad to put in my pin (which never existed in the first place). The pin I put in once is not working because I didn’t confirm it.

There is also a FaceID button but this does not work since the toggle is off. 

I was allowed to register FaceID without registering a pin and now I am locked out of the app.

DO NOT USE THEIR PASSWORD PROTECTION just use IOS 18’s FaceID.

Now I have no idea how to get my information back and might lose over a years worth of data.

The backups on my iCloud are from 2023.

title: Best Habit Tracker I’ve tried.
body:
I've been using Way of Life for a while now, and it's honestly been a game-changer in how I approach my daily habits. The app's design is clean and intuitive, making it incredibly easy to track my progress with just a few taps. Whether it's building new healthy habits or breaking old ones, Way of Life has empowered me to be more accountable and consistent. The unique color-coded system and the ability to see long-term trends are particularly motivating, pushing me to stay on track.

However, there's one feature I find myself wishing for - the ability to collaborate and share progress with friends or family. Many habit-tracking apps offer this social aspect, which can significantly boost motivation and accountability through shared goals and friendly competition. While Way of Life excels in personal habit tracking, adding a feature for collaboration and sharing could elevate the experience to new heights, fostering a sense of community and support among users.

In summary, Way of Life is an outstanding habit tracker that has made a noticeable difference in my life. It's straightforward, effective, and almost perfect. If you're looking to make meaningful changes in your habits, this app is definitely worth trying out. Here's hoping future updates might include the option to collaborate with others, making it not just a personal journey, but a shared one too.

title: The (Good) Habit-Forming App You Want!
body:
I've been looking for an app like this for a long time and I'm thrilled to finally come across Way of Life.

The closest I was able to find were the habit-forming apps by Jaidev Soin on the App Store. They looked great and did their job, but eventually they just became apps in the background that became 'too much of a hassle' to use (i.e. they didn't motivate me enough to stop being lazy).

Way of Life is incredibly easy to use, yet flexible enough to be customised to your personal needs and goals. Plus, something about being able to keep up those greens make me want to keep the trend going. Even if I didn't fulfill a goal / habit, there's a certain satisfaction to be gained from tapping on the checks, crosses and skips (perhaps it's all those colours).

If you're the type of person who wants to be productive, but sometimes needs motivation to stop being so lazy, then this could be the app you want. Double thumbs up!

Bug: When adding a note to the bottom entries (specifically when you have a lot of entries), the keyboard hides the note section so you can't see what you're typing. No other bugs / issues otherwise. Amazing app, thank you!

body:
I've used a half dozen different apps over the years to try and track habits. This is the first one that I've been really satisfied with. The UI is very good and gets out if your way after using it once or twice. It took me all of five minutes to set up the habits I want to track ( it has a selection of popular predefined habits  already available but you can also specify your own). It takes me on average a minute a day to update and review my progress.  It offers several views of the progress you've made on each habit through pie charts, bar graphs and trending lines. 
 Unlike other similar apps I've tried this one allows you to define habits your trying to avoid as well as those you are trying to form. It also allows you to go back to previous days and input data you may have missed after the fact. 
 This one sits on the home page of my iPhone.

title: Best of the Bunch
body:
I've tried almost all the food, exercise, and general tracking apps, and I can tell you this app is the best of the bunch.  It has programming finesse, an attractive and easy-to-use interface, and it's fully customisable. 

I'm using it to track lots of things: whether I lost weight, flossed, took vitamins, brought lunch to work, left work on time, exercised (good), ate sugar, ate refined grains, drank caffeine, drank alcohol (bad if more than one serving).  In the future, I might use it to track music practice, meditation, sleep, moods, stress, etc.  Over time, it's possible to see patterns and linkages between the items tracked. 

There is only one thing I would add to the app if I could, and that is a way to track when I do a thing more than once in a day. For example, I want to indicate (easily, with a click) each time I eat a serving of sugar, so that at the end of the day I know how many I've had. Right now, I can use notes to record servings, quantities, timings, reps, sets, distances, or whatever, which offers total flexibility. But it's not easy to see at a glance for each separate item tracked which days are better than others, and whether there's improvement over time. 

Programming the above would require a toggle to indicate which items are quantifiable, and then a separate, item-specific graph page to track and display quantities per day/week/month/year. 

Even without that functionality, though, it's a well-designed and useful tracking app. Highly recommended.
